blocks.text: Have you ever seen a map or a building plan? These are examples of scale drawings used to represent real-world objects on paper.

blocks.markdown: Scale drawing is a technique used to represent real objects or areas on paper using a specific scale. This means that every measurement on the drawing is proportional to the actual measurement of the object.

blocks.title: Definition of Scale Drawing
blocks.text: A scale drawing is a representation of an object or area in which all dimensions are proportional to the actual dimensions, based on a specific scale.

blocks.markdown: To create a scale drawing, you need to decide on a scale, such as 1 cm on paper representing 1 m in real life. This helps in accurately depicting large objects on smaller sheets.

blocks.title: Converting Real Length to Drawing Length
blocks.prompt: If a road is 100 meters long and the scale is 1 cm : 10 m, what will be the length of the road on the drawing?

steps.text: Identify the scale. Here, 1 cm represents 10 m.
Divide the real length by the scale factor: \( \frac{100}{10} = 10 \).

blocks.answer: The length of the road on the drawing will be 10 cm.

blocks.markdown: When reading a scale drawing, it's important to understand the scale used so you can accurately determine real distances from the drawing.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always double-check the scale used in a drawing before calculating any distances. Misreading the scale can lead to incorrect answers.

points: Scale drawings use a specific scale to represent real objects on paper.
Converting real lengths to drawing lengths involves dividing by the scale factor.
Understanding the scale is crucial for interpreting distances on a scale drawing.
